description: Whole fused MoE: route each token to its top-k experts, run gate/up and down projections, combine with the routing weights. Covers aiter fused_moe (CK/asm/FlyDSL 2-stage, including the sorting and quant kernels it launches) for bf16, FP8 block-scaled and MXFP4 weights.

inter_dim.doc: per-expert intermediate size on this rank (after TP split)

n_experts.doc: experts on this rank, including a fused shared expert if the deployment folds one in

topk.doc: experts per token, including the fused shared expert slot when there is one

layout.doc: the stored weight layout the dispatcher reads (w1/w2 is_shuffled, interleaved gate/up for SiTU-style kernels)

topk_ids.doc: override dist with load=observed and the per-expert token counts from the trace for timing buckets

hooks.moe_weights: (name, spec, shape, dtype, sym, gen, device) -> {w1, w2, and w1_scale/w2_scale when quantized: (stored, logical)}. Draw float weights (w1 ~ N(0, 1/model_dim), w2 ~ N(0, 1/inter_dim)) with `gen`, quantize them with the INSTALLED quantizer for `quant`, store them in `layout` with the installed shuffle (and set is_shuffled), and return as logical the float64 DEQUANTIZED, row-major, gate-rows-first weights. Scale shapes in the contract are placeholders for per-channel; for fp8 block scales or MXFP4 e8m0 scales override inputs.w1_scale.shape with a why.

call: Invoke the whole fused_moe entry as the model layer does (including expert_mask / num_local_tokens / doweight_stage1 when the deployment passes them) and return the combined output. The sorting kernel it launches is part of the boundary.

timing.cache: w1/w2 are weights and far larger than L2; read-evict matches serving. Routing decides which experts are touched: time on the observed expert load (routing.load = observed with per-expert counts from the trace), and if only uniform routing is available, report that bucket as a bound.
notes: decode buckets differ by up to 2.5x between uniform and skewed routing on the same shape

negative_controls: drop the routing-weight multiply in the stage-2 combine (or apply it twice): an unbiased-looking but large error the bound rejects
route one expert's tokens to expert e+1 in the gather: wrong rows, error ~ |out|
pitfalls: moe_sorting is nondeterministic for bit-identical inputs: build each case's args ONCE outside any repeat loop, or the routing metadata change reads as kernel nondeterminism. check_reproducible covers the operands, not the kernel's internal sort.

The installed kernel combines top-k with bf16 atomics, so two baseline runs differ; that is why the bound is baseline_relative with max_violation_fraction 1e-3 rather than an exact or tight-tol self comparison (a fail-count gate on that oracle is unpassable even for the baseline).
Uniform routing is the slow end of expert occupancy; it is fine for correctness, not for the served timing.
Count experts and top-k the way the deployment does: GLM-5.2 fuses the shared expert as expert 257 with topk 9; writing 256/8 makes every tuned lookup miss.
An MTP draft layer may run its MoE in bf16 (quant_type No) while the main layers are MXFP4: that is a separate task, not a case of this one.
Which language ran is printed by the 'using 2stage' dispatch line; the 'not found' line is printed only on a miss, so counting it inverts the conclusion.
